comments.content: `VULKAN_INTERNAL_CreateTexture` can return NULL (OOM / bind failure), but the new transition call runs *before* the `if (!texture) { return; }` guard below it. `VULKAN_INTERNAL_TextureTransitionToDefaultUsage` immediately dereferences `texture->subresourceCount`/`texture->subresources`, so a failed creation now crashes instead of bailing out. Move the transition after the NULL check. Also note the fresh texture is never tracked on `commandBuffer` (the old code tracked it in the throw-away barrier command buffer), so the recorded layout transition is not protected against the texture being destroyed before the command buffer completes — add a `VULKAN_INTERNAL_TrackTexture` (which also needs a matching untrack via the command buffer's `usedTextures` list, as done everywhere else).

Gating the whole cleanup section on `presenting` is a regression for workloads that never present (compute-only or offscreen-to-texture rendering): the fence-status loop that returns command buffers to the pool, the empty-allocation reclamation and `VULKAN_INTERNAL_PerformPendingDestroys` now only run when a swapchain present happens. Since `VULKAN_AcquireCommandBuffer` allocates a brand-new command buffer whenever the pool is empty (and `SDL_ReleaseGPUBuffer`/`SDL_ReleaseGPUTexture` etc. only queue into the pending-destroy lists), such an app grows `submittedCommandBuffers` and the pending-destroy lists without bound, and `defragInProgress` can stay set forever. The fence check itself is already safe for non-presenting submits, so keep the cleanup unconditional (as before) and only gate the defrag call on `presenting`.

Both new failure paths return early while `renderer->defragInProgress` and `commandBuffer->isDefrag` stay set. The only reset of `defragInProgress` happens in `VULKAN_INTERNAL_CleanCommandBuffer` when the command buffer it was recorded on is cleaned; if `VULKAN_Submit` fails after defrag (e.g. `EndCommandBuffer`/fence acquisition) or the buffer is never cleaned, `defragInProgress` stays 1 forever and the `!renderer->defragInProgress` guard permanently disables defragmentation. Clear both flags (and consider returning the partially-created resources) before returning here and in the texture branch. Additionally, the identical message in the texture branch below reports "defrag buffer" although a texture allocation failed, which makes OOM diagnostics misleading — word it as a texture there.

The new failure log in the texture branch of the defrag loop reuses the buffer message, so a texture allocation failure prints "Failed to allocate defrag buffer!". Since this is the only diagnostic for a texture OOM inside defrag, it is misleading. Use a texture-specific message, e.g. `SDL_LogError(SDL_LOG_CATEGORY_GPU, "%s", "Failed to allocate defrag texture!");` for this path.

That's factual and specific. Suggested fix: instead of relying on the transition being recorded on the caller's CB, record the "needs initial transition" state on the texture (e.g., a `transitioned` flag) and transition from UNINITIALIZED on first use. Actually, the layout tracking issue is inherent to any lazy/delayed transition. The old eager approach (separate submitted CB) had the property that the container's texture was in default layout as soon as it was inserted. Any deferred approach needs a per-texture "uninitialized" flag. SDL upstream actually added a `VulkanTextureSubresource.usageMode`? Not here.

Consider tracking this state on the subresource (e.g. a "needs initial transition" flag) and emitting the UNINITIALIZED barrier at first use rather than relying on the recording command buffer being submitted.
